content:
maria: Heads-up — saw a spike in spot evictions in us-east-1 this morning. Our a100-heavy pool lost ~18% capacity over 30m and the autoscaler couldn't refill fast enough.
alex: Oof. Did we lose specific instance classes or whole AZs?
maria: Mostly p4d and p4 instances. us-east-1a was the worst, but a slight uptick across b/c too. Eviction events spiked around 08:12-08:45 UTC.
infra-bot: [autoscaler] scaleDown: terminated 12 nodes in asg/llm-a100-spot-us-east-1a (reason: interruption), requestId=as-2026-06-12-08
k8s-bot: Pod reschedule: 84 pods evicted from node ip-10-0-12-45 (gpu=a100) during 08:12-08:50 UTC. Rolling reschedule started.
sanjay: Sounds like classic spot price churn. We should diversify instance classes and split critical low-latency routes to a small on-demand baseline. :thinking:
tera: (tagging tara) I mean tara — we already have fallback images, but latency for fallback CPU models is ugly. We need graceful degradation, not a hard fail.
tara: Yep. Two things: 1) more heterogeneous spot pools so evictions don't correlate, 2) preemptible handling in the scheduler so we move state before eviction. Recommend target: at least 4 distinct families across AZs with different bidding markets.
alex: For GPU families we can mix h100, a100, g5, l4 where feasible. But memory/perf differences are huge. We need a binpacking policy that groups pods by memory footprint and preferred perf class, and allow model-variant fallbacks when a faster GPU isn't available.
maria: Agreed. Experiment proposal: create "mixed-small" and "mixed-large" pools per region. Each pool: 10% on-demand baseline, 90% spot diversified across 4 instance types, cross-AZ. Set maxPrice to X for AWS where applicable.
ops-robin: FYI — some customers in EU have restrictions on spot usage. We'll need to gate by tenancy/contract. For public regions used by enterprise, require policy flag to disable spot fallback.
sanjay: Implementation sketch (ASG mixed instances policy):
```
mixedInstancesPolicy:
  instances: [p4d.24xlarge, p4d16xlarge, g5.16xlarge, g5g.12xlarge]
  onDemandBaseCapacity: 10
  onDemandPercentageAboveBaseCapacity: 10
  spotAllocationStrategy: "capacity-optimized"
```
This reduces correlated eviction and biases towards capacity.
tara: Add to that a scheduler hook. On termination notice we: drain node -> set pod annotation checkpoint=true -> trigger model checkpoint to S3 -> re-create pod on fallback pool if necessary. The drain window is small, so we should support incremental KV snapshots for long-running decoders.
alex: Also worth trying fractional GPU or multi-tenant inference on l4/rtx for low-memory models. That increases packing efficiency but adds noisy-neighbor risk. Keep it opt-in per route.
infra-bot: Action created: INFRA-764 diversify-spot-pools (assignee: sanjay)
maria: For metrics, add these new timeseries: spot_eviction_rate_by_pool, pod_fallback_rate, avg_inference_latency_fallback. If fallback rate > 5% in a region -> increase on-demand baseline.
ops-robin: Also track cost delta: goal is net cost <= current baseline - 12% while keeping p95 latency < 300ms for critical routes.
sanjay: I'll prototype mixed pools in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 next week. Plan: small traffic can be routed via traffic shadowing to measure p95 on various GPUs before shifting production.
tara: One more operational note: ensure CI images include graceful checkpointing hooks. Sample drain script: 
```
kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
curl -X POST https://checkpoint.internal/flush?pod=$POD_ID
sleep 8
```
We can make the flush call idempotent.
alex: Nice. Also add a fallback router policy: if realtime capacity < 20% for fast-gpu pool, route low-priority jobs to mixed-large, route interactive to on-demand baseline, and show degraded-mode banner in console.
maria: TL;DR — diversify instance classes + multi-AZ + small on-demand floor + eviction-aware drain & checkpoint + gradual rollout via shadowing. I'll update runbook if we greenlight. :thumbsup:
ops-robin: Sounds good. Please include a playbook for manual failover to dedicated capacity (redwood-dedicated) if spot collapse persists for > 2h.
sanjay: Will follow up with a PR detailing ASG/cluster changes and a spike experiment timeline.
infra-bot: INFRA-764 moved to In Progress by sanjay
alex: Thanks all — let's sync in the infra sync on Monday to pick a canary region and target metrics.
